newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Fighters to fly over Seoul in air defence drill.
newsitem.headline: Fighters to fly over Seoul in air defence drill.

text.p: South Korean fighter jets plan to make rare flights over the country's capital on Monday as part of efforts to improve military readiness in case of an attack by rival North Korea, military officials said on Sunday.
"The exercise has not been based on any specific situation, but is only one of routine military exercises," an official at the Joint Chiefs of Staff said by telephone.
South Korea's Yonhap News Agency said that in the drill, four fighter jets would pose as North Korean intruders in a test of the capital's radar and other equipment.
Yonhap, quoting unidentified military officials, said helicopters would also take part in the drill.
Similiar drills took place over the capital of Seoul in April and June.
The official at the Joint Chiefs of Staff said the exercise was planned mainly as part of the monthly civil defence drill, usually conducted on the 15th day of every month.
South Korea has been technically at war with communist North Korea since the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce instead of a peace agreement.
Tension has been high on the world's last Cold War frontier since a North Korean submarine landed 26 armed agents on South Korea's eastern coast of Kangnung in late September.
Twenty-four of the agents, who came ashore soon after their Shark-class submarine ran aground off the coast, have been killed or found shot dead. One has been captured alive and one is still missing.
Pyongyang has demanded the return of the bodies and the submarine, which it said accidentally drifted into South Korean waters when its engine failed.
South Korea insists Pyongyang should make an official apology for the incident before starting talks on the return of bodies and the submarine.
